# v1.1.0-dev.125: Virtual Windows, the edge cases

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.124`. This one is
all Virtual Windows. A study of where docking still went wrong turned up
the handful of causes behind most of the odd behaviour, and this release
works through them. The TDD has the measurements. This is what you'll
notice.

## Docking and undocking

- Dragging a window over a container and pressing Esc no longer docks it.
  Windows puts the window back on Esc, and WLM used to dock it anyway.
  Resizing a window by its edge over a container doesn't dock it either.
- A docked window no longer starts behind its container. It used to, until
  the next time you pressed the container, which is why a freshly docked
  window sometimes looked like it had vanished into the frame.
- A docked window's own dialogs stay above it. A docked app covered its
  own Save dialog before.
- Windows that can't be docked are refused up front, with a short notice:
  tool windows, dialogs that belong to another window, shell windows, and
  windows on another virtual desktop. An elevated window (an admin
  terminal, say) docks but WLM can't move it, and its pane now says so
  instead of turning into an unexplained blank.
- Closing a container from its taskbar button hides the group to the tray,
  the same as the X on its own title bar. It used to strand every docked
  window with its frame missing.

## While docked

- A docked window that gets snapped with Win+Arrow, nudged by its own app,
  or shoved off its pane some other way is put back, once. The container's
  bar says when one is off its pane. WLM tries three times and then leaves
  it, so an app that insists on placing itself can't fight forever.
- A docked window with a dialog open is left alone until the dialog
  closes. WLM used to resize it underneath its own modal.
- A window that refuses to shrink to its pane now teaches the splitter its
  minimum, with a "pane too small for this app" note, instead of spilling
  over its neighbour. A container also can't be shrunk below its own frame.
- Alt+Tab to one window of a minimized container brings the whole
  container back, not just that window.
- A container restored right after a maximize no longer leaves its windows
  at full-screen size.
- A display change while a container is minimized is remembered and
  applied when it comes back. Resume from sleep, unlocking, and a remote
  session reconnect each run one tidy-up pass.
- Dragging a splitter and letting go off the window, or a touch cancel,
  no longer saves a garbage ratio. The bar also tracks the cursor exactly
  now instead of drifting a few pixels near the ends.

## Fully docked

- Every real app tried (Calculator, Notepad, Windows Terminal, Electron,
  and a Chromium window under four GPU settings) draws live under full
  dock, so nothing is excluded. The list exists for the day something is.
- A window that already has its own window shape is left as an ordinary
  docked window rather than losing that shape.
- A fully docked app that hangs, or that hides its own window, shows a
  "not responding" or "hidden by its app" note on its pane rather than a
  frozen picture.
- The watcher that puts frames back if WLM dies now keeps trying for a
  minute on an app that was hung at that moment, and never touches a
  window that belongs to a newer WLM.

## Quit

Quitting WLM with the undock setting released every docked window the way
an explicit undock does, which rewrote the saved layout. A restart then
found every container empty. Quit now frees the windows and leaves the
layout alone, so the next start docks them again, the same as after a
crash.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
